launch-desk.title: Tidewell buys messaging app Murmurline for $3.2 billion
launch-desk.author: Inez Calder
body: [f01: Tidewell has agreed to buy the messaging app Murmurline.] [f02: The price is $3.2 billion.] [f03: Tidewell is paying entirely in cash, with no stock in the mix.]
[f04: Murmurline has 85 million monthly users.] That's the prize. Messaging is where people spend their time online, and Tidewell wants more of that time.
[f05: The companies expect the deal to close by mid-2027.] That's a long runway, and a lot can change before any money moves. Expect hard questions along the way, and a few nervous users.

byteward.title: Tidewell to buy messaging app Murmurline for $3.2 billion
byteward.author: Dana Whitlock
body: [f01: Tidewell is buying Murmurline, the popular messaging app.] [f02: The deal values Murmurline at $3.2 billion.]

[f04: About 85 million people use Murmurline every month.] Those users will be watching closely to see what changes under a new owner, and how soon. Messaging apps run on trust, and acquisitions tend to test it.

bench-and-bill.title: Tidewell agrees to buy Murmurline for $3.2 billion
bench-and-bill.author: Owen Brightwater
body: [f01: Tidewell has agreed to buy Murmurline, the messaging app.] [f02: The deal is worth $3.2 billion.] Getting it approved may be the hard part.
[f06: Tidewell already owns Skerry, a messaging app with 140 million users.] [f07: Two lawmakers have already asked antitrust regulators to take a close look at the deal.]

[f08: If regulators block it, Tidewell owes Murmurline a $250 million breakup fee.] [f09: Tidewell has also promised to keep Murmurline's end-to-end encryption.] That pledge seems aimed at the same regulators.

ohm-and-bit.title: Tidewell is buying Murmurline for $3.2 billion
ohm-and-bit.author: Rafe Okonkwo-Hart
body: [f01: Tidewell is buying the messaging app Murmurline.] For Murmurline's users, the big question is encryption.
[f10: Murmurline encrypts every message end to end, so only the sender and the recipient can read it.] [f09: Tidewell says Murmurline will keep that protection.]
[f11: Tidewell's own messaging app, Skerry, doesn't encrypt messages end to end.] [f12: Tidewell wants Murmurline and Skerry users to be able to message each other by 2028.]
That's where it gets hard: a chat between the two apps is only as private as its weaker end.

wirefold.title: Tidewell to acquire Murmurline for $3.2 billion
body: Tidewell has agreed to buy the messaging app Murmurline for $3.2 billion in cash, the companies said on Friday.
